SR-492.title: Review fees, systems abuse and automated decisions
SR-492.summary: Protection visa review upfront fee of $1,863.50; apparent transitional date discrepancy; no external consultation recorded; family courts recognise cumulative systems abuse; review scheduling constraints and improved court performance; parallel criminal investigation can serve distinct public interests; automated decision transparency; PBS affordability statement; NSW parliamentary retrieval discrepancy.

SR-493.title: Regional services, disability autonomy and NSW audit
SR-493.summary: NSW regional services inquiry recommends geographic reporting, unmet demand, travel and waiting standards, qualitative outcomes and regional funding. Supported decision-making and forensic tribunal inquiries identify participation barriers and limited reform evaluation. NSW audit reports $1.1 billion in uncorrected misstatements and $246 million on abandoned IT projects; these are not equivalent to theft. Other findings concern grid services, detention referral, Upper Macleay flood evidence and NDIA missing logs.

SR-494.title: Timely disclosure and infrastructure accountability
SR-494.summary: Departmental FOI records show publication intervals requiring reconciliation; third-party review rights are possible counter-evidence. NSW electoral report identifies $1.145 million in late donation disclosures. Essential Energy waiver requires equipment-level fault and repair reporting. ACMA preventive obligations, gas consultation records and NDIS evidence independence also examined. No deliberate concealment established.

SR-495.title: Aged care classification and Bellbrook landslip repairs
SR-495.summary: Technical Support at Home spreadsheet published but contents not examined. Seven-site flood repair sequence includes Armidale Road and Nulla Nulla Creek Road, Bellbrook, fifth and sixth. NDIS register shows apparent status/effective-date discrepancy. Riverina broadband, small business restructuring, APRA reporting, NDIS legislative applicability, energy consultation and budget statements examined.

SR-496.title: Cross-agency debt recovery and disaster rights
SR-496.summary: ART systemic notice identifies automated Family Tax Benefit debt offsets that did not consider repayment arrangements or hardship. ATO acknowledged shortcomings; inquiry and legislative proposals examined, final commencement unresolved. Human Rights Commission disaster report identifies prolonged essential-service disruption. NSW planning participation changes replace Kempsey statutory plan. Health practitioner fees and ANAO outsourcing target boundaries also examined.

SR-497.title: Legal correction and infrastructure quality
SR-497.summary: Administrative Review Council guidance requires automated administration to remain responsive to legal correction. Chaplin and Bendel judgments provide contrasting outcomes. Renewable investment and battery inspections examined separately: 61.19% substandard, 0.95% unsafe in reported random battery sample. Positive corrective measures retained. ANAO reporting confidence, ASIC warning and separate 14-site Armidale Road works examined.

SR-498.title: ICAC Operation Targo and institutional reform
SR-498.summary: ICAC identifies serious complaint-handling and cultural deficiencies, inadequate records and repeated failures to implement reforms, without individual corruption findings. Ten recommendations establish longer-term scrutiny. ANAO employee feedback identifies approval barriers. Regional airfares, historical child support collection audit and Telstra Super complaint explanations examined.

SR-499.title: Complaint populations and evidence preservation
SR-499.summary: OAIC release identifies 13 open complaints against itself and apparent 22-day age discrepancy requiring explanation. Macquarie admissions document $8.8 million remediation for 39,566 customers and daily website capture. Ombudsman assesses all 12 accepted NDIA assistive technology recommendations as implemented. Financial accountability reporting changes, Telstra Super judgment and Kempsey flood monitoring examined.

SR-500.title: Government redress and Kempsey election
SR-500.summary: Commonwealth Ombudsman financial remedies report identifies barriers to compensation, confidentiality and restrictive administration. ANAO identifies excluded beneficiary population in actuarial model, changed quality measures and suspended ASIC external review alongside alternative assurance. NSW complaint information utilisation, systemic detection, lending and employment advertising examined. Kempsey by-election reported for 16 January 2027.

SR-501.title: Commercial incentives and genuine evidence
SR-501.summary: ASIC Report 845 identifies referral conversion incentives and fear-based communication. AHRC synthetic media report identifies false acceptance and genuine evidence rejection. OAIC VIQ inquiry distinguishes contractual safeguards from compliance and closure from exoneration. Central Coast payment withdrawal costs require verification. Charity exemption, superannuation, biosecurity, housing and tribunal continuity examined.

SR-502.title: Kempsey financial oversight and judicial evidence
SR-502.summary: Draft minutes record capital pipeline motion lost 2–4, budget variations, CEO delegation and three financial policies. $90.1 million capital figure and underlying delegation instrument remain outstanding. Pryor, Neville and TechnologyOne judgments address evidence reliability, cumulative reputational harm and correction without unsupported culpability. Disability-sector employment remediation, emergency exemptions and electoral accessibility examined.

SR-503.title: FOI search integrity and regional mobile services
SR-503.summary: ANAO FOI audit identifies inadequate search documentation, missing advice and discrepancies in reported outcomes. OAIC disclosure-log review identifies timing and accessibility deficiencies. ACCC mobile services inquiry, aged care needs assurance, surviving licence obligations, prudential discretion and Kempsey project deferrals examined. No domestic roaming outcome established.

SR-504.title: AI-assisted complaints, missing data and delay
SR-504.summary: NSW Ombudsman recommends complaints be assessed on merits despite AI use. ASIC dashboard distinguishes nil reporting from missing submissions and technical validation from factual verification. APRA classification limits, financial reporting changes, Hollard insurance judgment, live cattle compensation and Kempsey proposed cemetery charge examined. Delay can amplify underlying harm.

SR-505.title: Executive accountability and accessibility
SR-505.summary: AIG court filings allege complaint handling failures; allegations not judicial findings. Bendigo Bank judgment establishes formal IT responsibility gap and $8 million penalty, with reimbursement and corrections. OAIC automation disclosure and breach severity, NSW cyber coordination, Kempsey parking restrictions, accessible toilet closure and disability inclusion examined.

SR-506.title: Environmental delegation and accessibility masking
SR-506.summary: Proposed NSW environmental approval agreement remains consultation, not operative authority. Optus privacy determination identifies 41,278 customers and untested cross-system responsibility assumptions. NSW Ombudsman case identifies clear AI-assisted communication obscuring accessibility needs. TAFE debt waiver, prenatal statutory tools, court disclosure, franchise costs, electricity and regional telecommunications examined.
